label: Existence in essence at an esse-essence identity: laws and models
paraphrase: Premise-free laws and finite models (structural surrogates, not metaphysical possibility). Laws: (1) Kant's conceptual thesis excludes conceptual containment of existence; (2) with concept adequacy it excludes, for every being, any essential truth entailing its existence; (3) with adequacy and the unconditional bridge 565ccd6c it excludes every esse-essence identity; (4) with the identity-to-concept bridge it excludes every esse-essence identity; (5) it yields contingency only when the represented space is identified with real possibility (access from w to every point) and the being has a nonempty concept; (6) existence-conditional essences, the act-fact link and exercise in the nature exclude every identity being whose absence is representable; (7) under the act-fact link every identity being's essence is exercised wherever it exists, so the conditional reading of exercise in the nature holds of every identity being; (8) constitutive essential existence implies the consequential form; (9) essence grounds necessity: a nature entailing existence gives necessity; (10) a contingent being's nature entails no existence; (11) within the essentialist framework (excluded middle, essence grounds necessity, the essentialist account of possibility, no other nature requiring x) an actual x's nature entails its existence if and only if x is necessary; (12) serious-actualist essences (every essential truth an unconditional predication) with essence grounds necessity and a nonempty nature give necessity. Models: kantAquinas (a necessary foundational identity being with the act-fact link, exercise in the nature, the unconditional bridge and constitutive essential existence, while Kant's thesis holds of a concept formed from its effects and neither adequacy nor the identity-to-concept bridge holds of it; its absence is representable but not really possible; for the concept adequate to its nature adequacy and the identity-to-concept bridge hold and Kant's thesis fails), conditionalIdentity (a contingent foundational identity being with the act-fact link, only conditional exercise in its nature, existence-conditional essences, the essentialist account, Kant's thesis and adequacy for the concept adequate to its nature), four omission models of the Kant-adequacy argument and two of the factorization of 565ccd6c.
